questions.stem: A deterministic Bug0 run has the following supplied event trace in a static environment: at obstacle hit H it enters boundary following; at L the goal heading becomes locally unblocked, so it leaves; the goal-directed segment returns it to the same hit state H. Sensor readings and the selected boundary-following direction then repeat. There is no stored-hit or loop-detection rule. What follows?
assumptions: The supplied event transitions are feasible for this example; static environment, unchanged goal and deterministic control; no extra loop detection.

options.text: The second visit automatically reverses the boundary-following direction and prevents another cycle.
The same H→L→H cycle can repeat; local leave eligibility alone does not establish progress to the goal.
Returning to H automatically reports the goal unreachable, as part of the stated Bug0 policy.
The second visit automatically triggers a full-perimeter search for the globally closest leave point.

questions.stem: A DQN learner’s bootstrap labels change whenever its online value estimates change. Which design choice most directly slows that particular moving-target feedback?

options.text: Shuffle stored transitions into replay minibatches while keeping bootstrap and online parameters identical at every update.
Compute bootstrap values with a separate network whose parameters are held or updated more slowly.
Use a separate action-selection estimate to reduce maximization bias, without specifying any slower target-parameter schedule.
Increase ε-greedy exploration while keeping bootstrap and online parameters identical at every update.

questions.stem: The online estimate Qθ(s,Right)=4.3, reward r=1.0, discount γ=0.9, and next-state target-network values are 3.0 and 5.0. For a nonterminal transition, let y=r+γ max Qφ(s′,a′) and δ=y−Qθ(s,Right). If the same transition were terminal, use no bootstrap term. Which tuple (nonterminal y, nonterminal δ, terminal y) is correct?
assumptions: Ordinary one-step DQN max target, not Double DQN; terminal means zero remaining bootstrap value; all Q/reward values use the same reward scale.
